findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile a40f's dependency direction: either the harness scores only committed reply text through a pluggable/imported new parser (declaring depends_on df3a and 4ca2), or split the harness so the 'new parser' scoring arm is sequenced after the parser children land.
evidence: a40f approach: 'score deterministically: parse success under the current parser vs the new selection+sentinel parser'
a40f deps: [] (no depends_on df3a or 4ca2)
4ca2 deps include depends_on a40f; 18ae deps include depends_on a40f — both order a40f earlier
df3a builds selection in parse_structured; 4ca2 builds the sentinel marker extraction — the 'new selection+sentinel parser' does not exist until both land
findings.finding: a40f's harness scores replies 'under the current parser vs the new selection+sentinel parser', but the new parser is produced by df3a (selection) and 4ca2 (sentinel); a40f declares no depends_on df3a or 4ca2, while 18ae and 4ca2 both declare depends_on a40f — ordering a40f before the parser it must exercise. The live-run scoring's 'new parser' arm is under-sequenced.
scenarios: The workflow_dispatch harness run (a40f's operator-attested AC) executes before df3a/4ca2 land, so its 'new parser' scoring arm has no new parser to invoke and can only score the current parser — or a40f's live code imports parser behavior that is not yet present.
findings.suggested_fix: Have a40f declare depends_on df3a and 4ca2 for the live 'new parser' scoring arm (keeping its offline scorer unit tests on committed E2 goldens dep-free), and adjust the epic sequencing so the harness before/after run that 4ca2/18ae attest against runs after the parser is in place.

findings.finding: Three children (df3a, 4ca2, a40f) each declare the SAME fixtures directory tests/fixtures/structured_reply_corpus in file_impact, but no child owns its creation, and both df3a's and a40f's plan-review attestations were signed asserting the directory is absent (created by them) — an implicit-shared-state collision when landed independently.
scenarios: Whichever of df3a/a40f/4ca2 lands second finds the corpus directory already present when its verified-at-sha state and attestation assumed 'absent', or the two children commit divergent/duplicated E2 fixture files that must be reconciled at merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Designate df3a as the corpus creator (it lands first in the selection chain); have 4ca2 and a40f append their E2 fixtures under a documented sub-layout and re-attest with the corpus recorded as present rather than 'dep absent'.

'add exact-id measured-fact capability rows only for cells a live measurement passed'

The design-investigation and E1–E4 experiment comments on the bug child record the derisking evidence, not the durable contract/decision a future maintainer needs when a routine model swap re-triggers the class.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the deterministic PASS/FAIL threshold (the score or predicate on the harness artifacts) that qualifies a model cell for native structured output.
evidence: 'Every model cell measured PASS runs native structured output and every unmeasured or failing cell stays prompted with a recorded reason'

'Before/after raw-output distributions ... as recorded, deterministically scored artifacts' — the scoring is deterministic but the PASS/FAIL boundary that drives the rows child's native-vs-prompted decision is not stated
This is a data-design ambiguity under E2 signal (2): the acceptance criterion (what makes a cell eligible for native output) is implicit
findings.finding: The 'measured PASS' threshold that gates which model cells go native vs stay prompted is referenced by both the rows child and the harness child but the plan never states what score/criteria constitutes a cell PASS.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — rows child ('Every model cell measured PASS runs native structured output') and harness child ('deterministically scored artifacts')
scenarios: An executor lands the rows child and must decide whether a marginal cell (e.g. 98% valid extraction) counts as PASS with no stated threshold
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to the rows/harness ACs defining PASS, e.g. 'a cell PASSes when the harness scores 100% schema-valid native extraction across the fixture corpus with zero decoy wins.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the guard child with structured.py:53 / ADR-0059: state that measured gating still forces PromptedOutput whenever the CALL has thinking on (the 400 is per-call, not a stale per-model relic), and reframe 'stale blanket thinking guard' accordingly.
evidence: structured.py:49-55 'pairing extended thinking with a native/forced output constraint is the documented Anthropic 400 ... a property of the CALL, so the caller's thinking argument is authoritative ... not a relic of any earlier forced-tool mechanism'
ADR-0059:102-103 'output mode ... with thinking forcing PromptedOutput regardless'
The AC frames per-MODEL 'thinking-compatibility' measurement, but the 400 is documented as a per-CALL property independent of the model's supports_thinking flag (structured.py:53)
findings.finding: The guard child's AC characterizes output_mode's thinking->PromptedOutput fork as a 'stale blanket thinking guard' to be replaced by measured call-property gating, but the code and ADR document it as a LIVE per-call Anthropic 400 constraint, not stale — loosening it for measured-native cells could regress thinking-on calls.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (guard child): 'output_mode gates native output on measured thinking-compatibility per model instead of blanket-forcing prompted'; Approach thrust 2
scenarios: A model cell measured native-PASS is later invoked with thinking=on; the loosened guard selects NativeOutput and the call 400s (the documented 'Thinking may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use').
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the guard-child AC as 'output_mode gates native output on measured native-safety per model, AND continues to force PromptedOutput whenever the call has extended thinking enabled (the documented Anthropic 400 is a per-call property)'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the SDK child's version floor and the eval/aiobotocore conflict in the SAME package terms (boto3, matching pyproject's conflicts block and risk bullet) — or explicitly justify why botocore is the right axis and give both the botocore floor and its corresponding boto3 floor.
evidence: pyproject.toml:261-262 '[eval] -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore pins boto3 < 1.40.62 while pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock] >= 1.107 ... needs boto3 >= 1.42.63'
AC quotes a botocore floor ('botocore >= 1.43') while the conflict it references (~line 261) and the risk bullet are expressed as boto3 pins
botocore and boto3 are separate distributions with non-identical version numbers
findings.finding: The SDK child AC states the floor as 'botocore >= 1.43', but the pyproject conflicts block and the plan's own risk bullet reason in boto3 version terms (boto3 >= 1.42.63 vs the eval/aiobotocore cap boto3 < 1.40.62); botocore and boto3 are distinct packages with distinct version lines, so the floor and the conflict it must keep resolvable are stated in mismatched units.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (SDK child): 'The locked Bedrock SDK accepts Converse outputConfig client-side (botocore >= 1.43)'; Risks: 'the botocore floor collides with the [eval] -> aiobotocore cap'
scenarios: Implementer pins/locks botocore>=1.43 but the eval/aiobotocore fork is capped on boto3, so the 'uv tree version proof' cannot be checked against a single package and the fork-resolvability check named in the risk targets the wrong distribution.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to the SDK child a parameter-level verification that the pinned botocore's Converse API actually accepts `outputConfig` (observe it in the botocore service model / a recorded live Converse probe), classifying the evidence Verified rather than relying only on `uv tree` installability.
evidence: Plan asserts 'The locked Bedrock SDK accepts Converse `outputConfig` client-side (botocore >= 1.43)' but the stated check is only 'lock resolution and a recorded `uv tree` version proof' — a version-installability proof, not an API-surface proof.

ADR-0059 records Bedrock currently runs `native_structured_output=false` with PromptedOutput ('despite native_structured_output=false on the Bedrock profile, the run emitted a fully-formed verdict envelope — PromptedOutput is sufficient'), so native Bedrock structured output is a NEW, previously-unused integration surface for rebar.

botocore/boto3/pydantic_ai BedrockConverseModel + BedrockModelSettings all resolve as installed, but the repo file tools cannot read site-packages to confirm the `outputConfig` parameter, and `search_files outputConfig` returns no repo match — the parameter existence at the asserted floor is UNVERIFIED, not observed.

Flag/parameter-level empiricism: an installable botocore version does not guarantee its Converse action accepts `outputConfig` (parameter-name/version mismatch causes silent runtime failure after ship).
findings.finding: The SDK/rows/guard children depend on the Bedrock Converse API accepting an `outputConfig` parameter client-side at `botocore >= 1.43`, but neither the plan nor its stated verification confirms that this specific wire parameter exists at that floor — the AC's check (`uv tree` version proof + lock resolution) proves the version is installable, not that its Converse surface accepts `outputConfig`.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'The locked Bedrock SDK accepts Converse outputConfig client-side (botocore >= 1.43) ... checked by lock resolution and a recorded uv tree version proof'; Risks — 'Bedrock rejects outputConfig for opus-4-7/4-8 server-side'
scenarios: The SDK floor resolves and `uv tree` proof passes, but the pinned botocore's Converse client rejects `outputConfig` as an unknown parameter, so the native path 400s/ValidationErrors on every measured-PASS cell.
A later botocore introduced `outputConfig` under a different key/shape than assumed, so the rows-child native cells fail at runtime despite passing the version proof.
findings.suggested_fix: In the SDK-child AC, augment the check from 'lock resolution + uv tree version proof' to also include an observed parameter proof — e.g. a recorded probe that the locked botocore's `bedrock-runtime` Converse operation model lists `outputConfig` (or a live minimal Converse call round-tripping it), so the claim is Verified (observed) not merely installable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the sentinel channel's concrete marker (the exact delimiter/token the directive instructs the model to emit and the extractor matches) and state how it reconciles with schema_directive's existing 'no prose, no markdown fence' instruction so the two co-located directives do not conflict.

ABSENCE: the plan states the channel's existence and atomic shipping but never names the marker the model must emit / the extractor must match, nor whether it supersedes or conflicts with the existing 'no prose, no markdown fence' directive
findings.finding: The 'sentinel output channel' names a new directive+extraction contract but never defines the sentinel marker's concrete value/shape, nor reconciles it with the existing schema_directive instruction 'Respond with ONLY a single JSON object ... no prose, no markdown fence' — a directive an added sentinel delimiter would contradict.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('explicit sentinel output channel whose extraction ships in the same change as the directive'); Approach thrust 1 (sentinel child)
scenarios: The sentinel directive tells the model to wrap the payload in a delimiter while the co-resident schema directive still forbids fences/prose, producing contradictory instruction-locality guidance the model resolves unpredictably
The extractor and the directive disagree on the exact sentinel token because the plan pinned neither, so extraction silently misses the channel
